placementQuiz.explain: 5 detail rows + 1 grand total row = 6 rows total.

blocks.md: ROLLUP = hierarchical ladder (detail → subtotals → grand). CUBE = full cross-product (all combinations). GROUPING SETS = pick your own adventure. GROUPING() tells you which level you're on.

items: ROLLUP: N+1 levels (N columns + grand total)
GROUPING SETS: explicit list, most flexible
GROUPING() + GROUPING_ID() distinguish detail vs subtotal rows

blocks.label: rollup examples
blocks.code:
-- Single column: detail + grand total
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id);
-- Result: 5 dept rows + 1 grand total (dept_id=NULL)

-- Two columns: detail + subtotals + grand
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, status);
-- Hierarchy: (dept,status) → (dept) → ()

-- Partial rollup
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id, ROLLUP(status);
-- Detail (dept,status) + (dept) subtotals + grand total
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: ROLLUP supported
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, status WITH ROLLUP;
blocks.py-pandas:
# ROLLUP via pivot_table margins
df.pivot_table(index=['dept_id', 'status'], values='id', aggfunc='count', margins=True)

items.q: ROLLUP(a, b, c) produces how many grouping levels?
items.explain: ROLLUP: N columns = N+1 levels. (a,b,c) + (a,b) + (a) + () = 4 levels.

items.q: GROUP BY a, ROLLUP(b) vs GROUP BY ROLLUP(a, b):
items.explain: GROUP BY a, ROLLUP(b) = (a,b) + (a). GROUP BY ROLLUP(a,b) = (a,b) + (a) + ().

blocks.label: cube examples
blocks.code:
-- Full cross-tab
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY CUBE(dept_id, status);
-- Groups: (dept,status), (dept), (status), ()

-- CUBE with 3 columns = 8 combinations
SELECT a, b, c, COUNT(*)
FROM t
GROUP BY CUBE(a, b, c);
-- (a,b,c), (a,b), (a,c), (b,c), (a), (b), (c), ()
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: CUBE supported
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, status WITH CUBE;
blocks.py-pandas:
# CUBE via multiple pivot_tables
import itertools
results = []
for r in range(3):
    for cols in itertools.combinations(['dept_id', 'status'], r+1):
        results.append(df.groupby(list(cols)).size().reset_index(name='count'))
pd.concat(results)

blocks.label: grouping sets
blocks.code:
-- Only dept subtotals + grand total (no status subtotals)
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((dept_id, status), (dept_id), ());

-- Only status subtotals
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((status), ());

-- Equivalent to CUBE but explicit
SELECT dept_id, status, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((dept_id, status), (dept_id), (status), ());
blocks.py-pandas:
# Manual GROUPING SETS
sets = [['dept_id', 'status'], ['dept_id'], ['status'], []]
results = [df.groupby(cols).size().reset_index(name='count') for cols in sets]
pd.concat(results, ignore_index=True)

items.explain: Explicit list: (a,b) detail + (a) subtotal. Grand total () must be explicit.

blocks.label: grouping functions
blocks.code:
-- GROUPING(col): 1 if col is NULL due to rollup, 0 if detail
SELECT dept_id, status,
  GROUPING(dept_id) AS g_dept,
  GROUPING(status) AS g_status,
  COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, status);

-- GROUPING_ID: bitmask of GROUPING() values
SELECT dept_id, status,
  GROUPING_ID(dept_id, status) AS gid,
  COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY CUBE(dept_id, status);
-- gid: 0=detail, 1=status rolled, 2=dept rolled, 3=grand total

-- Pretty labels
SELECT 
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept_id)=1 THEN 'ALL DEPTS' ELSE dept_id END AS dept,
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(status)=1 THEN 'ALL STATUS' ELSE status END AS status,
  COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, status);
blocks.py-pandas: # No direct equivalent; use margins + detect NaN in index

options: dept_id is NULL in source data
items.explain: GROUPING(col) = 1 when col is NULL because it was rolled up (subtotal/grand total).
Bit 0 = status rolled, Bit 1 = dept rolled. 11 = both = grand total.

sections.title: Worked Problem — Department × Status Report with Labels

blocks.text: Problem: Cross-tab with labeled subtotals and grand total

items.title: Department Subtotals + Grand Total
items.statement: Employee count per department with subtotals and grand total. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count, level.

approaches.name: Brute
approaches.idea: UNION ALL of three separate queries: detail, dept subtotals, grand total.

code.code:
-- Detail rows
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, 'detail' AS level
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id, job_title

UNION ALL

-- Dept subtotals
SELECT dept_id, NULL AS job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, 'dept_subtotal' AS level
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id

UNION ALL

-- Grand total
SELECT NULL AS dept_id, NULL AS job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, 'grand_total' AS level
FROM employees

ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: same syntax with WITH ROLLUP
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count,
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept_id)=1 THEN 'grand_total' WHEN GROUPING(job_title)=1 THEN 'dept_subtotal' ELSE 'detail' END AS level
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id, job_title WITH ROLLUP
ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.py-pandas:
detail = employees.groupby(['dept_id', 'job_title']).size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
detail['level'] = 'detail'
subtotal = employees.groupby('dept_id').size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
subtotal['job_title'] = None
subtotal['level'] = 'dept_subtotal'
grand = pd.DataFrame({'dept_id': [None], 'job_title': [None], 'emp_count': [len(employees)], 'level': ['grand_total']})
pd.concat([detail, subtotal, grand]).sort_values(['dept_id', 'job_title'])

approaches.cost: Three full scans of employees + UNION ALL merge. O(3n) time. Manual labeling error-prone.
approaches.pitfalls: Must manually maintain ORDER BY across UNION. NULL handling in ORDER BY varies by DB. Easy to miss a grouping level.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: ROLLUP — single scan, engine builds all grouping levels internally, GROUPING() for labels.

code.code:
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count,
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept_id)=1 THEN 'grand_total'
       WHEN GROUPING(job_title)=1 THEN 'dept_subtotal'
       ELSE 'detail' END AS level
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, job_title)
ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.mysql:
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count,
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept_id)=1 THEN 'grand_total'
       WHEN GROUPING(job_title)=1 THEN 'dept_subtotal'
       ELSE 'detail' END AS level
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id, job_title WITH ROLLUP
ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.py-pandas:
detail = employees.groupby(['dept_id', 'job_title']).size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
detail['level'] = 'detail'
subtotal = employees.groupby('dept_id').size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
subtotal['job_title'] = None
subtotal['level'] = 'dept_subtotal'
grand = pd.DataFrame({'dept_id': [None], 'job_title': [None], 'emp_count': [len(employees)], 'level': ['grand_total']})
pd.concat([detail, subtotal, grand]).sort_values(['dept_id', 'job_title'])

approaches.cost: Single scan + internal grouping sets computation. Engine optimizes shared work across levels. O(n) time.

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept_id)=1 THEN 'grand_total' WHEN GROUPING(job_title)=1 THEN 'dept_subtotal' ELSE 'detail' END AS level FROM employees GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, job_title) ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;

items.title: Dept × Job Title Cross-Tab
items.statement: Full cross-tabulation: dept × job_title with all subtotals. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count.

approaches.name: Brute
approaches.idea: UNION ALL of four queries: detail, dept subtotals, job_title subtotals, grand total.

code.code:
-- Detail
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, job_title
UNION ALL
-- Dept subtotals
SELECT dept_id, NULL, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id
UNION ALL
-- Job title subtotals
SELECT NULL, job_title, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY job_title
UNION ALL
-- Grand total
SELECT NULL, NULL, COUNT(*) FROM employees
ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.mysql: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, job_title WITH CUBE ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.py-pandas:
detail = employees.groupby(['dept_id', 'job_title']).size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
dsub = employees.groupby('dept_id').size().reset_index(name='emp_count'); dsub['job_title'] = None
jsub = employees.groupby('job_title').size().reset_index(name='emp_count'); jsub['dept_id'] = None
grand = pd.DataFrame({'dept_id': [None], 'job_title': [None], 'emp_count': [len(employees)]})
pd.concat([detail, dsub, jsub, grand]).sort_values(['dept_id', 'job_title'])

approaches.cost: Four full scans + UNION ALL. O(4n) time. Manual NULL placement for subtotals.
approaches.pitfalls: Easy to forget a combination (e.g., job_title subtotals). ORDER BY across UNION is fragile.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: CUBE — single scan computes all 2^N combinations. Engine shares work across grouping sets.

code.code:
SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count
FROM employees
GROUP BY CUBE(dept_id, job_title)
ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.mysql: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, job_title WITH CUBE ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;
code.py-pandas:
detail = employees.groupby(['dept_id', 'job_title']).size().reset_index(name='emp_count')
dsub = employees.groupby('dept_id').size().reset_index(name='emp_count'); dsub['job_title'] = None
jsub = employees.groupby('job_title').size().reset_index(name='emp_count'); jsub['dept_id'] = None
grand = pd.DataFrame({'dept_id': [None], 'job_title': [None], 'emp_count': [len(employees)]})
pd.concat([detail, dsub, jsub, grand]).sort_values(['dept_id', 'job_title'])

approaches.cost: One scan + optimized grouping sets. Engine computes all combinations in one pass. O(n) time.

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY CUBE(dept_id, job_title) ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;

items.title: Partial Rollup: Dept + Job Title Subtotals Only
items.statement: Detail (dept,job_title) + dept subtotals. No grand total. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count.

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id, ROLLUP(job_title) ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;

items.title: GROUPING Bitmask Logic
items.statement: Compute bitmask: 0=detail, 1=job_title rolled, 2=dept rolled, 3=grand. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count, gid.

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, (GROUPING(dept_id) * 2 + GROUPING(job_title)) AS gid FROM employees GROUP BY CUBE(dept_id, job_title) ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;

items.title: Custom Grouping Sets: Dept Only + Job Title Only
items.statement: Show dept subtotals and job_title subtotals, but no detail rows. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count.

exercise.solution: SELECT dept_id, job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((dept_id), (job_title), ()) ORDER BY dept_id, job_title;

items.title: Pretty Subtotal Labels
items.statement: Replace NULL in subtotal rows with 'TOTAL' or 'ALL'. Return dept_id, job_title, emp_count.

exercise.solution: SELECT COALESCE(dept_id::text, 'ALL DEPTS') AS dept, COALESCE(job_title, 'ALL JOBS') AS job_title, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, job_title) ORDER BY dept, job_title;

blocks.claim: GROUPING(col) = 1 means the same as col IS NULL in the result.
blocks.refutation: GROUPING(col) = 1 only when col is NULL because it was rolled up (subtotal/grand total). If col is NULL in the source data, GROUPING(col) = 0 for detail rows. They are not equivalent.
blocks.correctModel: Use GROUPING() to detect subtotal rows. Use col IS NULL to detect source NULLs. They serve different purposes.

evidence.label: proof on hr data
evidence.code:
SELECT dept_id, status, GROUPING(dept_id) AS g_dept, GROUPING(status) AS g_status
FROM employees
GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept_id, status);
-- Subtotal rows have g_dept=1 or g_status=1
-- Source NULLs in status would show g_status=0 for detail rows

revisionCard: ROLLUP = N+1 levels (detail → subtotals → grand); CUBE = 2^N combinations
GROUPING SETS = explicit list of grouping combinations; most flexible
GROUPING(col) = 1 when col is NULL due to rollup (subtotal row)

glossary.def: Hierarchical grouping: detail rows + progressive subtotals + grand total.
Cross-tabulation: all 2^N combinations of grouping columns.
Explicit list of grouping combinations to include.
Returns 1 if column is NULL due to rollup (subtotal), 0 if detail row.
Bitmask of GROUPING() values for multiple columns. Bit i = GROUPING(col_i).
A row produced by ROLLUP/CUBE/GROUPING SETS that represents a subtotal or grand total.
